chose: admin auth isolated by three independent mechanisms: own admin Postgres schema, own ADMIN_BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, own buttery-admin.* cookie prefix
over: a shared better-auth instance with a role column on public.user
separate tables in the public schema with an admin_ name prefix only
reusing the app's BETTER_AUTH_SECRET across both apps
because: cookies ignore ports, so 127.0.0.1:3000 and :3100 are ONE jar — under the default prefix, signing into the admin signs you out of the app and vice versa. Verified end-to-end: one browser context now holds buttery-admin.session_token and better-auth.session_token side by side, an atproto sign-in and an operator sign-in, neither disturbing the other. A shared secret would let a token minted by either app verify against the other, making the table split decoration.

chose: revision history captured by a Postgres AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on public.atproto_collection_recipe writing into admin.atproto_record_revision
over: teaching services/atproto-cron-sync to write a second table
fetching real repo history from atproto per record
because: atproto exposes no per-record revision endpoint — history lives in the commit log (com.atproto.sync.getRepo / the firehose), which the sweep does not read. So what is available is OBSERVED history, at sweep granularity, and the UI says so (backfill rows are marked backfill, not created). A trigger captures every writer for free — the sweep, a backfill script, a hand-run UPDATE during an incident — instead of putting a second writer on the sweep's hot path. Cost is one INSERT per CHANGED record; an unchanged re-sweep writes nothing. down() removes trigger and function, leaving the app's write path exactly as it was. All 254 of web's DB tests pass with it installed.

chose: the record detail view never resolves local vs network into one answer — it shows both columns and labels the disagreement
over: picking a winner the way the app's read path does
because: the app already resolves, and that resolution is precisely what hides the bug an operator is looking for. A local copy that has drifted from what the user actually published is invisible from either side alone. Deciding what to do about a 'differs' row is a human's job; this tool's job is to make the disagreement visible.

chose: admin migrations live in services/web named <timestamp>_admin_<description>, and web's db:codegen now excludes admin.*
over: a second kysely-ctl migration pathway in services/admin
because: asked for explicitly, and it is the right first move: one migration runner, one ordering, no risk of two clocks stamping conflicting prefixes. The admin_ sub-prefix is what makes them greppable as a group when they do move out. Web's DB types stay ignorant of the admin schema via an exclude-pattern brace glob; the admin's own codegen includes both, so admin tables surface as "admin.admin_user" keys in its DB interface.
